summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, chronic steroid use, bilateral corneal transplants, and multiple comorbidities was admitted following sudden onset of right retro-orbital headache and right eye vision changes, including red desaturation and blurriness, after a brief loss of consciousness. Initial evaluation at an eye specialty center prompted transfer for further neurological assessment. Imaging including CT head, MRI brain and orbits, and MRA of head and neck showed no acute intracranial abnormality, mass, or vascular dissection. Laboratory studies were stable, with normal renal function and potassium. The clinical picture was most consistent with right optic neuritis, likely related to his underlying autoimmune condition. Pain was managed conservatively, and no changes were made to his chronic medications, including dexamethasone and azathioprine. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with neurology and ophthalmology, to start outpatient terbinafine for a fungal infection, and to monitor for worsening symptoms. Pending blood tests include fungal cultures, RPR, and ACE levels.
